<r>Sir 5:1-5</r>
<n>1</n> Noli atténdere ad possessiónes iníquas, et ne díxeris: Est mihi suffíciens vita; nihil enim próderit in témpore vindíctæ et obductiónis.
<n>2</n> Ne sequáris in fortitúdine tua concupiscéntiam cordis tui,
<n>3</n> Et ne díxeris: Quómodo pótui? aut quis me subíciet propter facta mea? Deus enim víndicans vindicábit.
<n>4</n> Ne díxeris: Peccávi, et quid mihi áccidit triste? Altíssimus enim est pátiens rédditor.
<n>5</n> De propitiáto peccáto noli esse sine metu, neque adícias peccátum super peccátum.

<n>4</n> Say not: I have sinned, and what harm hath befallen me? for the most High is a patient rewarder.

<r>Sir 5:6-11</r>
<n>6</n> Et ne dicas: Miserátio Dómini magna est, multitúdinis peccatórum meórum miserébitur;
<n>7</n> Misericórdia enim et ira ab illo cito próximant, et in peccatóres réspicit ira illíus.
<n>8</n> Non tardes convérti ad Dóminum et ne dífferas de die in diem;
<n>9</n> Súbito enim véniet ira illíus et in témpore vindíctæ dispérdet te.
<n>10</n> Noli ánxius esse in divítiis iniústis; non enim próderunt tibi in die obductiónis et vindíctæ.
<n>11</n> Non véntiles te in omnem ventum et non eas in omnem viam; sic enim omnis peccátor probátur in dúplici lingua.
<r>Sir 5:12-16</r>
<n>12</n> Esto firmus in via Dómini, et in veritáte sensus tui, et sciéntia; et prosequátur te verbum pacis et iustítiæ.
<n>13</n> Esto mansuétus ad audiéndum verbum, ut intéllegas, et cum sapiéntia próferas respónsum verum.
<n>14</n> Si est tibi intelléctus, respónde próximo; sin autem, sit manus tua super os tuum, ne capiáris in verbo indisciplináto et confundáris.
<n>15</n> Honor et glória in sermóne sensáti; lingua vero imprudéntis subvérsio est ipsíus.
<n>16</n> Non appelléris susúrro, et lingua tua ne capiáris et confundáris.

<r>℟.</r> Ut sciam quid accéptum sit coram te omni témpore.

<r>44th Discourse on the Words of the Lord</r>
<c>T</c>hat her son was called again to life was the joy of that widowed mother; that souls of men are every day called to life is the joy of our Mother the Church. He was dead in body they have been dead in mind. His death was outward, and was outwardly bewailed; their inward. Death hath been neither mourned for nor seen. But He hath sought for them, Who hath seen that they are dead, and He only hath seen that they are dead, Who hath been able to make them alive. If He had not come to raise the dead, the Apostle had not said: “Awake, thou that sleepest, and arise from the dead, and Christ shall give thee light.” <n>Eph. v. 14.</n>

b.e5c4d30b19:
<h>Martyrology</h>
<c>A</c>ugust 30th 2027, the 28th day of the Moon, were born into the better life:
<h>A</h>t Rome, upon the Ostian Way, under the Emperors Diocletian and Maximian, the blessed Priest Felix. After being racked he was sentenced to be beheaded as he was being led to execution he was met by some man who of his own accord professed himself a Christian, and was accordingly forthwith beheaded along with him. The Christians never knew the name of this other, and they accordingly always spoke of him as him who was added, that is, added to the company of the holy martyr Felix in winning of the crown.
<h>L</h>ikewise at Rome, the holy Virgin and martyr Gaudentia, with three others.
<h>A</h>t Sfaitla, in Africa, [in the year 399,] sixty blessed martyrs, who were slain by the fury of the Gentiles.
<h>A</h>t Bologna, [in the year 1026,] the holy Abbot Bononius.
<h>A</h>t Rome, [in the year 410,] also the holy Priest Pammachius, [a Roman Senator,] who was eminent for his teaching and holiness.
<h>A</h>t Susa, also in Africa, [in the year 250,] holy Boniface and Thecla, who were the parents of twelve sons, all blessed martyrs.
<h>A</h>t Thessalonica, the holy Confessor Fantinus. He suffered much from the Saracens, and was thrust out of the monastery wherein he had lived in marvellous austerity. He led many into the path of salvation, and at length fell asleep in a good old age.
<h>A</h>t Meaux, [in the year 670,] the holy Confessor [Fefrash, an Irishman, who came over into Gaul, where he is called] Fiacre, [and founded a monastery, and died towards the end of the seventh century.]
<h>A</h>t Trevi, [near Subiaco, towards the middle of the eleventh century,] the holy Confessor Peter, famous for many graces and miracles, who there passed away to be with the Lord, and is held in honour and worship.
<r>℣.</r> And elsewhere many other holy martyrs, confessors, and holy virgins.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.

<r>Luc 7:11-16</r>
<c>I</c>n illo témpore: Ibat Iesus in civitátem, quæ vocátur Naim: et ibant cum eo discípuli eius et turba copiósa. Cum autem appropinquáret portæ civitátis, ecce, defúnctus efferebátur fílius únicus matris suæ: et hæc vídua erat, et turba civitátis multa cum illa. Quam cum vidísset Dóminus, misericórdia motus super eam, dixit illi: Noli flere. Et accéssit et tétigit lóculum. - Hi autem, qui portábant, stetérunt - Et ait: Adoléscens, tibi dico, surge. Et resédit, qui erat mórtuus, et cœpit loqui. Et dedit illum matri suæ. Accépit autem omnes timor: et magnificábant Deum, dicéntes: Quia Prophéta magnus surréxit in nobis: et quia Deus visitávit plebem suam.
<r>℣.</r> Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nostri.
<r>℟.</r> Deo grátias.
Commemorátio Fratrum, Sorórum, Familiárium, Benefactórum defunctórum Ordinis nostri.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

Per Christum Dóminum nostrum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.4cb51e3d4b:
<h>Regula vel Evangelium</h>
<r>℣.</r> Grant, Lord, a blessing.
May the divine assistance ✠ remain with us always.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
<c>t</c>o Luke
<r>Luke 7:11-16</r>
<c>A</c>t that time, Jesus went to a town called Naim; and His disciples and a large crowd went with Him. And as He drew near the gate of the town, behold, a dead man was being carried out, the only son of his mother, and she was a widow; and a large gathering from the town was with her. And the Lord, seeing her, had compassion on her, and said to her, Do not weep. And He went up and touched the stretcher; and the bearers stood still. And He said, Young man, I say to you, arise. And he who was dead, sat up, and began to speak. And He gave him to his mother. But fear seized upon all, and they began to glorify God, saying, A great prophet has risen among us, and God has visited His people.
<r>℣.</r> But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.
<r>℟.</r> Thanks be to God.
Commemoration of the deceased Brethren, Sisters, Relations and Benefactors of our Order.
Requiéscant in pace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>Psalm 116</r>
§11.0a67a14e81
<r>℣.</r> Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.
<r>℟.</r> As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Show us, O Lord, thy mercy.
<r>℟.</r> And grant us thy salvation.

<r>℣.</r> O Lord, hear my prayer.
<r>℟.</r> And let my cry come unto thee.
<c>D</c>irect, we beseech thee, O Lord, our actions by thy holy inspiration, and carry them on by thy gracious assistance: that every prayer and work of ours may always begin from thee, and by thee be happily ended.
Through Christ our Lord.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

<r>℣.</r> Our help is ✠ in the name of the Lord,
<r>℟.</r> Who made heaven and earth.
<n>Si non sequitur aliqua Hora dicitur</n>
<r>℣.</r> May the souls of the faithful, through the mercy of God, rest in peace.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.

b.8ed4d5e9ba:
<h>Oratio</h>
<r>℣.</r> Dóminus vobíscum.
<r>℟.</r> Et cum spíritu tuo.
<c>O</c>rémus.
<c>E</c>cclésiam tuam, Dómine, miserátio continuáta mundet et múniat: et quia sine te non potest salva consístere; tuo semper múnere gubernétur.
<h>P</h>er Dóminum nostrum Iesum Christum, Fílium tuum: qui tecum vivit et regnat in unitáte Spíritus Sancti, Deus, per ómnia sǽcula sæculórum.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
b.ca2359c1fc:
<h>Prayer</h>
<r>℣.</r> The Lord be with you.
<r>℟.</r> And with thy spirit.
<c>L</c>et us pray.
<c>O</c> Lord, we beseech thee, let thy continual pity cleanse and defend thy Church, and because it cannot continue in safety without thy succour, preserve it evermore by thy help and goodness.
<h>T</h>hrough Jesus Christ, thy Son our Lord, Who liveth and reigneth with thee, in the unity of the Holy Ghost, God, world without end.
<r>℟.</r> Amen.
